## 開場固定收益論點

Christopher Waller將市場原本認定的聯準會9月升息，改寫為取決於通膨走勢的條件式反應。美國公債溫和牛市趨陡：2年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.34%，10年期與30年期則各下降2個基點，分別收在4.77%與5.25%。2s10s與2s30s曲線均陡峭化3個基點，分別至43個與91個基點。這種型態顯示壓力緩解集中在政策路徑，並非前一週推升殖利率的期限溢價全面消退。

這波緩解幅度可觀，卻不完整。2年期與5年期殖利率單週仍上升14個基點，10年期仍上升10個基點，30年期也上升6個基點。Waller表示，若通膨持續朝2%目標改善，聯邦基金利率目標可望維持在3.50%-3.75%；若通膨再度加速，仍可能需要升息。本週稍早，交換市場估計升息1碼的機率約70%；他發言後，機率降至約五五波。收盤走勢消化了部分近期緊縮溢價，卻不能證明聯準會的通膨問題或較高的均衡資本成本已經過去。

當日經濟數據說明長端為何只有有限度跟漲。8月ISM服務業指數由54.1升至55.4，新訂單升至60.9，支付價格則升至72.6。就業指數仍處於萎縮區間的47.8；需求增強與投入成本上揚並存，難以作出全面偏鴿解讀。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.42%，10年期損益兩平通膨率卻上升1個基點至2.35%。WTI收於$91.79，布蘭特原油收於$95.91；儘管單日漲幅已大幅縮小，單週仍分別上漲近10%與7%。投資人下修了近期政策反應預期，卻未下修能源與服務業帶來的通膨風險。

風險資產也反映這種區別。S&P 500上漲1.06%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.16%，VIX則降至14.32。美元指數下跌0.59%至5月以來最低，黃金期貨大漲3.65%至$4,525.70。美國投資級債與高收益債利差大致持平，硬通貨新興市場債利差小幅收窄。跨資產走勢更像是政策焦慮獲得釋放，而不是市場認定名目成長或信用品質突然改善。

因此，兩個時間軸仍彼此衝突。若下一批通膨數據證實近期降溫，Waller的近期反應函數容許聯準會耐心觀望；他同時指出，美國公債的安全價值正在減弱、財政壓力加重，人工智慧投資又競逐資本，意味中性利率更高、長端溢價更持久。週四收盤僅暫時解答第一個問題，第二個問題仍反映在5.25%的長債殖利率中。

## Waller以通膨為政策轉折關鍵

Waller的訊號比泛泛而談數據依賴更具影響力，因為他改變了目前傾向的政策選項。他形容政策僅略具限制性，也承認通膨仍顯著高於目標，包括7月PCE年增率達3.7%。即使如此，由於能源成本上升尚未廣泛擴散至其他價格，他預期下一批消費者與生產者物價報告應屬溫和。他也指出，若在通膨開始下降之際緊縮，政策可能踩錯時點。綜合而言，只要通膨持續降溫，按兵不動就是可信的基準情境；若8月數據顯示改善逆轉，升息選項仍然保留。

限制條件與政策傾向同樣重要。Waller未提供明確的通膨數值門檻，只表示小幅再加速也可能使他轉向更緊縮的政策。7月決策有三位政策官員反對，主張升息25個基點；主席Kevin Warsh在Jackson Hole的談話，也曾使市場將升息視為大概率事件。Waller只是在立場明顯分歧的委員會中加入另一個具影響力的觀點，並非代表共識已定。與9月決策連結的合約重新定價，升息1碼機率降至約50%，至年底的預期緊縮幅度也由一度高達41個基點降至34個基點。

服務業活動提高了債市續漲門檻。ISM指數55.4高於約54.2的預估，並創六個月最強擴張訊號。新訂單上升3.7點至60.9，為2023年2月以來最高；支付價格上升2.3點至72.6。供應商交貨指數由52.8降至51.3，但仍連續21個月高於50。S&P Global服務業PMI終值由54.6升至56.5，需求訊號與ISM一致，但低於56.8的初值。

調查中的勞動市場遠弱於需求。即使訂單激增，ISM就業指數仍低於擴張門檻，報47.8。截至8月29日當週，初領失業救濟金人數僅增加2,000人至206,000人，前一週則修正為204,000人。四週平均升至207,250人；續領人數增加8,000人至177.9萬人，其四週平均則減少5,000人至178.175萬人。裁員尚未明顯升高，但招聘指標疲弱，聯準會雙重使命中的就業面仍足以牽制升息。

7月貿易報告帶來另一種成長歧義。商品與服務貿易逆差由修正後的$712億擴大24.4%至$886億。出口減少$66億或2.1%至$3,107億，進口增加$108億或2.8%至$3,993億。商品逆差擴大至$1,196億，服務盈餘則微升至$310億。逆差擴大可能拖累國內生產毛額，但組成並不單純代表最終需求疲弱：資本財進口大增$144億，其中電腦與電腦配件分別增加$69億與$66億。這份報告一方面指向淨出口貢獻轉弱，另一方面也顯示科技設備投資需求持續。

Waller對較長期前景的評論，使前端漲勢不能直接延伸為完整的存續期間投資論點。他將美國公債殖利率部分升勢歸因於市場憂心美國財政狀況、AI基礎建設競逐資本，以及政府債券原有的安全與流動性溢價減弱。這些力量促使他上調中性利率估值，意味同一政策利率對需求的抑制可能低於以往假設。他估計聯邦債務約$40兆，2026財政年度赤字接近GDP的6%，並主張除非結構性赤字更接近零，否則單靠成長無法實質降低債務負擔。

上述判斷也限制了債務管理操作的效果。Waller認為，即使長天期美國公債買回規模加倍，也不會帶來太多持久緩解；9月將進行首筆至少$40億的操作。買回可改善舊券流動性，卻無法消除長端對財政、通膨與資本競爭所要求的補償。當日殖利率曲線也呈現相同區別：2年期殖利率對政策傾向反應最大；10年期與30年期只下降2個基點，且仍遠高於一週前。

現券市場交易集中在反應函數變化最大的區段。名目附息債券按原始面額計算的交易量達$8,657億，較前一交易日增加6.1%。2年期以下到期券種的交易量增加31.1%至$2,017億，3年以上至5年期區段增加16.4%至$2,432億。雙向成交量無法辨認買賣方，卻顯示交易量增幅最大的是對9月與年底政策重新定價最敏感的券種。

## 日本央行政策支撐日圓升勢

日圓上漲2%至1美元兌155.52日圓，背後出現比官方再度干預更持久的解釋。據報日本央行官員傾向將目前1%的政策利率上調25個基點，且認為經濟變化尚不足以支持升息50個基點；若通膨上行風險延續，9月之後的步調仍保有彈性。交換市場已近乎完全反映升息1碼，並估計12月再次升息的機率約80%。空頭回補與國內避險放大了匯率走勢，但新增資訊關乎央行的基準路徑與後續行動，不只是交易員擔心官方進場。

日本央行帳戶資料提供了排除性證據。央行預估其經常帳餘額將因財政因素減少¥4,100億，貨幣經紀商原估約減少¥7,000億。兩者差額遠低於¥7,290億，也就是2022年以來最小規模的干預，因此官方再度大舉買進日圓的可能性偏低。日本在上一輪干預行動投入¥15.4兆後，這項確認尤其重要：原先被視為可能由官方行動推動的走勢，主要其實來自市場對貨幣政策與部位的重新定價。

官方施壓仍協助塑造了這輪定價。財務大臣片山皋月表示，日本對匯率仍抱持同等緊迫感，也反映首相高市早苗的看法；但她強調，美國財政部長Scott Bessent在雙方會面時並未提出絕對要求。日本央行審議委員高田創先前不排除更大幅度或連續升息，已使市場預期的可能路徑更為分散。目前的澄清使首次行動更集中於25個基點，但未排除後續加快升息。正因標準幅度升息已高度反映在價格中，若完全不升息，市場衝擊反而更大。

30年期日本公債標售顯示，殖利率升高可吸引國內需求，卻不能為超長端利率劃定上限。投標倍數為3.79倍，低於前次3.86倍，但高於12個月平均的3.52倍。結果公布前，30年期殖利率一度下降10個基點至4.065%，期貨在公布後仍維持漲勢。需求廣度足以避免投資人原先擔憂的疲弱結果。

標售品質並非全面強勁。標售尾差由0.21擴大至0.28，顯示平均得標價格與最低得標價格的落差加大。買方願意承接殖利率高於4%的供給，但尾差擴大，表示市場尚未就日本央行政策正常化與財政不確定性所需的補償取得平衡。即使壽險業者認為4%已具投資價值，創紀錄的支出要求與進一步升息前景，仍使風險集中在超長端。

政府年金投資基金近期釋出的訊號，代表潛在需求來源，而非配置已經調整。管理委員會於8月21日開會，是七年來首次公開宣布在8月召開會議；就在五個月前，該基金才認定無需檢討投資組合，如今又重新檢視運作事項。這檔¥318兆基金對國內債券、外國債券、日本股票與海外股票的目標配置仍各為25%。自3月以來，10年期JGB殖利率已上升約1個百分點並一度突破3%，重新考慮國內債券權重的可能性因而提高。這次會議本身不能證明GPIF已調整目標。

對美國公債的中期影響除了直接資產配置，也會透過匯率避險傳導。截至6月30日，日本、加拿大、台灣等六個市場的大型投資人只避險41%的外幣曝險，為至少2015年以來最低。以這些市場共計$4.6兆的曝險計算，避險比率提高5個百分點，將代表約$2,300億的交易。對日圓投資人而言，3個月期美元避險成本已由2023年10月的6%降至2.75%；日本投資人上半年新購外債的避險比率則為41%，低於2024年的62%。

這些部位並未造成週四美國公債上漲，調查也只涵蓋全球持債的一部分；然而，若日本央行緊縮使利差縮小，且美元不再於市場避險時期提供緩衝，這些部位將產生不對稱風險。日本投資人可保留美債、同時遠期賣出美元，因此增加避險未必等於立即出售美債；但當國內JGB殖利率競爭力提高時，這可能削弱美元資產的匯兌報酬，並改變增持外國存續期間曝險的邊際效益。

## 能源風險拉高各地不同政策門檻

歐洲進入供暖季時，能源緩衝異常不足。即使只要達到歐盟最低75%的儲氣目標，仍需補充逾100太瓦時、按現價計算價值超過€70億的天然氣。若要達標，注氣速度必須達到2022年能源危機以來從未在如此晚季節出現的水準。天然氣價格三天上漲10%後持穩，但低庫存使歐洲容易受到寒冷天候、中國積極採購、管線停擺或美國液化天然氣供應中斷衝擊。即使原油單日漲勢放緩，這項實體限制仍使歐洲存續期間部位保有通膨溢價。

歐洲央行近期行動更為確定，終點卻仍有爭議。最新調查的65位經濟學家全數預期，下次會議將把存款利率調升25個基點至2.50%，高於8月調查的83%；約91%預期年底利率為2.50%，78%預期利率將維持在此水準至2027年中。相較之下，利率期貨反映這次升息之後還有一次升息。分歧不在近期方向，而在能源帶動的通膨衝擊是否會持續到足以延長升息循環。

8月活動與價格數據為這項分歧保留空間。歐元區服務業PMI僅由51.7微降至51.6，綜合指數持平於52.0。製造業需求抵銷海外服務業務轉弱，使整體出口訂單四年半來首次增加。服務業就業以八個月最快速度成長，帶動2026年首次出現單月民間部門淨增就業。服務業投入成本與產出價格均升至三個月高點，綜合產出價格通膨也停止下降。整體通膨率達3.3%、通膨降溫停滯，足以支持市場預期的升息，卻都無法單獨證明市場反映的下一次升息必然成真。

英格蘭銀行首席經濟學家Huw Pill從等待成本切入，描述同一波能源衝擊。他主張提早調升銀行利率，可避免暫時性通膨壓力轉為持久，並降低日後更激進緊縮的必要。Pill是7月主張升息的三位貨幣政策委員會成員之一。期貨反映9月升息1碼的機率略高於15%，11月以前升息的機率則超過70%。他的發言擴大了採取行動的理由，卻未顯示委員會已就時點形成共識。

英國存續期間資產已因殖利率處於歷史高檔而吸引新買盤。Freetrade債券平台週二的購買筆數與金額均創2026年最高，Hargreaves Lansdown也錄得5月15日以來英國公債買盤最熱絡的一天。2056年到期、票息5.375%的債券，以及2028年與2061年到期的低票息債券均屬交易最活躍券種。散戶投資人持有的流通債券仍低於4%，這股資金無法獨力承接主權債市，卻顯示全球拋售後，10年期殖利率約5.2%、30年期接近5.8%，正吸引重視稅務效益的家庭投資需求。

馬來西亞的鷹派轉向較細微，卻已實際發生。馬來西亞國家銀行如22位經濟學家中20位所料，將隔夜政策利率維持在2.75%，但刪除對政策立場「適當」的描述；自2025年9月以來，每次決策均曾使用這個詞。令吉交換市場將未來12個月的緊縮定價增加14個基點，累計升息50個基點的機率升至近50%；決策前，市場只反映接近一次25個基點升息。2026年成長接近5%，其中第2季達6%；若7月僅1.8%的低迷通膨被更強需求或能源成本轉嫁取代，央行有空間因應。

土耳其8月通膨數據的邊際變化方向相反。年通膨率由31.8%放緩至31.5%，略低於31.6%的市場共識；月通膨率雖由1.78%微升至1.84%，仍低於1.92%的預估。2年期里拉債券殖利率下降14個基點至39.6%。資金成本已由實際40%正常化回到37%的政策利率，降息因而更為可能；但核心通膨僵固、能源壓力再現、通膨預期轉弱，使立即寬鬆仍具爭議。即使整體通膨持續降溫，同一波使ECB與BOE保持警戒的油價衝擊，也可能延後土耳其降息。

波蘭與匈牙利使區域政策路徑進一步分化。波蘭政策官員Iwona Duda表示，3.75%的利率可能在2026年剩餘時間維持不變，即使遠期協議已反映未來12個月約三次各1碼升息。8月通膨升至14個月高點3.4%，接近2.5%目標容忍區間的上緣；燃料價格上限到期與肥料成本上升，可能將通膨推至區間之上。Duda認為沒有立即緊縮必要，但否定近期降息預期。

據報匈牙利準備在連續三次各降息25個基點後暫停，基準利率將維持5.5%，同時把通膨目標由3%下調至2.5%。目標調整強化新政府推動歐元接軌的政策方向，福林兌歐元一度升值1.5%，政府債券殖利率則下降。7月通膨率僅1.2%，提供下調目標而無需立即緊縮的空間。然而，2026年預估預算赤字達GDP的7.5%，Fitch又關注可信的債務路徑，因此債券反應仍取決於財政落實，而非只看通膨目標。

澳洲顯示全球存續期間衝擊可壓過國內差異。截至週三的一個月，10年期殖利率上升約30個基點至15年高點5.25%，漲幅超過同業；即使三大評等機構均給予AAA評等，且公共債務低於美國與英國，仍未能避免。3月外資持有51%的政府債務，高於一年前的46%；經避險主權債指數2026年仍上漲0.3%，優於美國公債下跌0.7%與全球政府債下跌0.6%。較佳信用品質可支撐相對表現，但澳洲利率與美國利率高度相關，在全球通膨與供給溢價穩定前，市場仍將承受壓力。

## 巴基斯坦重啟主權融資窗口

巴基斯坦完成目前最明確的案例，證明低評等主權國家仍可進入硬通貨市場。該國以兩批債券籌得創紀錄的$30億：5年期$17.5億、殖利率7.75%，以及10年期$12.5億、殖利率8.25%。訂單接近$60億，發行推介期間風險溢價收窄約25個基點。即使Moody's的B3評等仍低於投資級六個級距，發行殖利率仍大致符合相近評等主權債。

資金用途比亮眼訂單更重要。巴基斯坦面臨約$220億的外部融資需求，計畫償還成本高昂的短期債務、延長到期年限並降低再融資風險。阿拉伯聯合大公國在連續七年展期後，近期拒絕再展延$30億，巴基斯坦因此必須改由沙烏地阿拉伯提供支援。巴基斯坦也要求中國為$13億商業貸款再融資；中國是其最大債權國，未償餘額超過$250億。該國並考慮在三年融資策略中發行伊斯蘭債券與人民幣債券。已完成的交易以定期市場債務取代部分雙邊存款依賴，卻未消除更廣泛的外部融資需求。

整體收盤走勢也反映這種區別。硬通貨新興市場債利差小幅收窄，巴基斯坦2031年到期債券微升至99.65美分。信用評等調升與IMF計畫改善了市場准入，全球高收益債溢價接近數十年低點也有利執行。在7.75%-8.25%殖利率下，訂單仍接近發行額兩倍，反映核心政府債殖利率居高不下時，改革進展所需付出的融資價格。

印度面對相反問題：外幣資金動員造成國內流動性過剩。銀行透過獎勵計畫吸收創紀錄的$1,270億外幣非居民存款，若計入相關外幣貸款則超過$1,360億。資金流入支撐盧比，並為銀行提供成本較低的存款基礎；但與印度儲備銀行直接換匯，使銀行體系流動性升至創紀錄的9.7兆盧比，約合$1,026.6億。由於流入資金遠超過至少$800億的初始目標，計畫已於8月31日提前一個月結束。

銀行主管目前提議以美元兌盧比賣出買回交換交易吸收剩餘流動性，而非提高現金準備率。最長一年期的交換交易，可對應印度儲備銀行遠期部位中估計將於一年內到期、約$450億的美元空頭部位。這項工具可在展延外匯曝險的同時吸收盧比；另有出售債券與提高準備率等選項。銀行反對調升準備率，因為此舉將壓縮利差。最終工具選擇將決定過剩流動性是支撐貨幣市場與債券，還是透過外匯帳簿沖銷。

菲律賓則顯示，貨幣走弱可能限制原定的本幣供給。財政部正重新評估一筆5年期巨額債券，原計畫納入9月共3,800億披索的發行。通膨已連續三個月放緩，但7月仍達6.2%，超過年度目標兩倍；中東衝突推高油價之際，披索也跌至歷史新低。9月有超過1,000億披索散戶國庫債券到期，10月另有500億披索到期；取消大型發行將使再融資與市場流動性更為困難，繼續發行則會鎖定更高利息支出。最近一次5年期標售的需求只有發行額1.2倍，低於前次相同年期標售的3.1倍。

委內瑞拉違約債券上漲，因可用於重整的潛在資源基礎出現變化。一項協議使美國取得超過650億桶已探明儲量的控制權後，2027年到期主權債升至每美元54美分，接近四個月高點。若計入尚未支付的應計利息，目前價格顯示回收率低於債權的三分之一。分析師認為，日產量可能在一至兩年內達150萬桶；Chevron則已承諾五年投資$70億，使其委內瑞拉產量增加逾一倍。

這項重整仍可能成為史上最大規模的主權債務重整。有估算指出，若納入PDVSA商業債務與本幣債務，總求償額可能高達$2,290億；政治轉型情境下的潛在減記幅度為26%，政權延續情境則達83%。目前債券漲勢反映未來美元收入機率提高，並不代表市場已就債務可持續性、債權人範圍或投入資本達成共識。政府尚未揭露回收模型的分母，石油投資就已先改善分子。

IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva點出這些個別成功案例的系統性限制。她警告，先進經濟體殖利率上升、能源通膨持續，以及AI發債競逐資本，可能逆轉低所得與新興市場債務可持續性的改善。她仍形容市場秩序良好，並將Senegal視為加快二十國集團共同框架努力的檢驗。巴基斯坦成功發債、印度流動性過剩，以及委內瑞拉回收前景改善，均顯示資本依然可得；如今，比單一新興市場beta更重要的是資金條件與到位途徑。

## 沉重供給暴露最弱資產負債表

即使融資日程更加吃重，美國整體信用利差仍未變動。投資級債平均殖利率超過5.5%，利差在一週大部分時間仍低於80個基點。交易商對9月發行量的預估中位附近為$2,150億，高於一年前創下的單月紀錄$2,075億；個別預估介於約$1,900億至$2,500億。2026年前八個月中有四個月創下單月紀錄，最近三個月均包括在內。美國公債殖利率偏高，促使2027年有融資需求的借款人趁利差補償仍受控時提前籌資。

壓力不只來自整體承接能力，也來自投資人集中度。科技公司為持續擴大的AI建設融資，反覆出現的大型交易使個別發行人在基準投資組合中的權重提高。許多投資級投資委託將單一公司權重限制在3%-5%。即使最大型科技借款人仍低於門檻，另一個發行沉重的月份也可能迫使投資人將新增曝險與日益增加的替代標的比較。因此，即使整體利差穩定，當投資組合已承接大量供給後，後續進場發行人的成交門檻仍會上升。

ByteDance證明銀行仍具備大規模承作能力。該公司最初尋求$200億貸款，最終取得$296億美元貸款，成為2026年亞洲第2大美元借款。銀行承諾踴躍，推動最終規模提高；資金將用於加速AI投資計畫。這是一筆最終規模顯著擴大的已完成融資，不只是科技借款人有意擴大支出的證據。

其他發行人正分散融資幣別與證券。Public Storage完成以C$12億收購68處加拿大設施後，正洽談約C$5億的7年期債券，初始利差約為加拿大政府債券加95個基點，將是該公司首次以加幣融資。其美國優先無擔保債務評等為A2/A。風險光譜另一端的AirAsia則表示，最高$10億國際債務與7億令吉本地融資將用於再融資成本高昂的疫情期間債務，而非填補營運虧損。

AirAsia現有債務結構說明為何仍須檢視上述區別。該公司4月安排一筆以航線收入擔保的$2.3億私募信貸債券，2024年另向Ares等基金借入$4.43億，票息最高達11%。缺乏燃油避險、又難以將航空燃油成本上升轉嫁給價格敏感旅客，導致單季淨損5.27億令吉，創四年最大。再融資可延長到期年限並降低利息負擔，卻仍須面對營運現金流轉弱，以及自伊朗戰爭開始以來股價下跌64%的考驗。

Cerba Healthcare已從準備再融資進入法院監督程序。這家由EQT支持的檢驗公司，在貸款人已形容其資本結構不可持續後，針對約€50億債務申請法國調解程序。淨負債超過€49億，相當於過去12個月獲利的9倍；6月底現金約€1.08億。贊助股東提供€1億貸款補充流動性，債權人則將利息支付寬限期延至11月。第2季EBITDA成長約12%至逾€1.22億，營收成長2%至€4.69億，但這些改善尚未修復槓桿，也未解決法國醫療給付費率的不確定性。

CSN呈現相反案例：公司治理變動提高市場對去槓桿的信心。擔任執行長逾二十年的Benjamin Steinbruch立即卸任並轉任董事長，由Vale前主管Fabio Schvartsman接掌營運。CSN正尋求透過出售水泥與基礎建設持股籌得約$29億。2030年到期、票息11%的債券上漲2.25美分至80.5，股價一度上漲20%。市場反應顯示，投資人更相信資產出售與資本結構修復會落實，並不代表債務已經減少。

市政借款人顯示，專用收入與營運壓力可在同一市場內分歧。紐約大都會運輸署公布一筆$7.85億發行案，以售價至少$200萬房地產的交易稅為擔保。這項稅收預計2026年帶來近$4億收入，2027年至2030年每年約$3.5億；新債發行後，年度債務服務約為$1.5億。Moody's給予該結構A1評等，S&P近期則調升至AA-。這筆交易將用盡相關證券年度本金與利息的法定上限，因此核心保障來自質押稅基，而非MTA整體營運。

Chicago最新預測使壓力更直接落在營運收支。市長Brandon Johnson預估，債券付款、生活成本調整、大宗商品通膨與稅增融資盈餘下降將推升支出，使2027年公司基金出現$8.82億赤字。包含擬出售債務催收權在內的措施，收入不如預期，使本期預算仍有$8,500萬缺口。市府計畫明年額外提撥$3.64億退休金，並運用再融資節省金額與疫情時期剩餘準備金處理眼前缺口。這些措施可提供流動性，卻沒有指出填補更大2027年缺口所需的經常性收入。

中國境內評等結構造成另一種利差不透明。在超過6,500家信用債發行人中，近90%的國內評等達AA或以上，美國相同比例僅4.4%。S&P指出，一家全球評等為B、所屬類別5年累計潛在違約率達15.34%的發行人，發行熊貓債時可能獲得AAA評等。中國人民銀行自4月起要求本地評等機構降低最高評等集中度，已促使評等下調與撤回。即使外國借款人仍可在總值37兆人民幣的市場取得資金，更有效的評等區分也可能擴大發行人之間的利差分化。

這些交易說明美國利差指數為何仍持平，卻不能將持平等同所有發行人的融資條件一致。ByteDance擴大銀行貸款，Public Storage開拓新幣別資金池，MTA則有專款專用的稅收質押。AirAsia必須在獲利疲弱時再融資，Cerba於法院監督下協商，CSN依賴資產出售能否執行，Chicago則仍有未解決的營運缺口。基準殖利率對所有發行人都相同；抵押品、專用收入、受償順位與現金流生成能力，決定哪些資產負債表能承受這項成本。

## 前瞻市場意義

9月4日美東時間上午8:30公布的8月就業報告，是Waller條件式耐心能否承受勞動數據意外的第一關。非農就業人數預估在前值減少23,000人後增加56,000人，失業率預估維持4.1%，平均時薪月增率預估由0.1%升至0.3%。招聘疲弱且薪資持平或放緩，將強化2年期美債漲勢，使9月決策進一步偏向按兵不動；若就業增幅或薪資高於預期，尤其失業率維持不變，服務業需求訊號將重新連結至升息理由。

接下來一週，通膨與存續期間承接能力將同時面臨考驗。9月10日公布的整體與核心生產者物價月增率均預估為0.3%，9月11日接續公布8月消費者物價。美國財政部3年期、10年期與30年期標售，以及預期回升的公司債供給，將在通膨結果仍未明朗時，顯示投資人是否接受目前殖利率。物價上漲廣度溫和且標售有序，可使聯準會近期耐心與結構性期限溢價的區分延續；非能源通膨僵固或投標疲弱，則會使政策與供給風險重新交織，即使就業成長放緩也會限制長端漲幅。

全球存續期間資產將透過兩家不同央行，面對共同的政策順序考驗。市場普遍預期ECB將在9月10日把存款利率調升25個基點至2.50%；針對能源與服務價格是否需要進一步行動的指引，將顯示市場定價與經濟學家預期一次升息後停止的路徑，何者更接近管理委員會立場。BOJ在9月18日面對更鮮明的二元結果，因升息1碼已近乎完全反映。若按標準幅度升息，並對後續行動保留可信彈性，可望支撐日圓，也將檢驗JGB需求能否承接政策正常化而不再次外溢全球；若延後行動，或指引排除後續升息，將動搖日圓漲勢的政策基礎，並使本週帳戶資料已排除的干預風險再度浮現。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Christopher Waller turned a September Federal Reserve increase from the market's presumed next step into a conditional response to inflation. Treasuries rallied in a modest bull steepening: the 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.34%, compared with 2-basis-point declines in the 10- and 30-year yields to 4.77% and 5.25%. The 2s10s and 2s30s curves each steepened 3 basis points, to 43 and 91 basis points. That shape is consistent with relief concentrated in the policy path, not a broad retreat from the term premium that had lifted yields during the preceding week.

The relief was meaningful but incomplete. The 2- and 5-year yields remained 14 basis points higher over one week, the 10-year was still up 10 basis points and the 30-year up 6 basis points. Waller said continued progress toward 2% inflation could justify leaving the 3.50%-3.75% federal-funds target unchanged, whereas renewed acceleration could still warrant a hike. Swaps moved from roughly 70% odds of a quarter-point increase earlier in the week to about even odds after he spoke. The close removed part of the near-term tightening premium; it did not establish that the Fed's inflation problem, or the higher equilibrium cost of capital, had passed.

The day's economic evidence explains why the long end offered only a limited follow-through. The August ISM services index rose to 55.4 from 54.1, new orders reached 60.9 and prices paid climbed to 72.6. Employment remained in contraction at 47.8, but the combination of stronger demand and firmer input costs resisted a uniformly dovish reading. Ten-year real yields fell 3 basis points to 2.42%, while 10-year breakeven inflation rose 1 basis point to 2.35%. WTI closed at $91.79 and Brent at $95.91, leaving them almost 10% and 7% higher over one week despite much smaller daily gains. Investors marked down the immediate policy response without marking down the inflation risk carried by energy and services.

Risk assets embraced the distinction. The S&P 500 rose 1.06%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.16% and the VIX fell to 14.32. The Dollar Index declined 0.59% to its lowest level since May, while gold futures surged 3.65% to $4,525.70. U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed, and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly. The cross-asset move looks like a release of policy anxiety rather than a judgment that nominal growth or credit quality suddenly improved.

Two horizons therefore remain in conflict. Waller's near-term reaction function allows patience if the next inflation readings validate recent moderation. His separate diagnosis of eroding Treasury safety value, fiscal pressure and competition for capital from artificial-intelligence investment points to a higher neutral rate and a more persistent long-end premium. Thursday's close resolved the first question only provisionally and left the second embedded in a 5.25% long bond.

## Waller Makes Inflation the Hinge

Waller's signal was more consequential than a generic appeal to data dependence because it altered the choice he is presently leaning toward. He described policy as only slightly restrictive and acknowledged that inflation remains materially above target, including a 3.7% year-over-year PCE reading in July. Even so, he expects the next consumer- and producer-price reports to be reasonable because higher energy costs have not yet spread broadly into other prices. He also identified the risk of tightening just as inflation begins to fall. That combination made a hold his plausible base case under continued moderation, while preserving a hike if August data show that progress has reversed.

The qualification matters as much as the lean. Waller supplied no numerical inflation threshold and said only a small acceleration might move him toward tighter policy. Three policymakers dissented from the July decision in favor of a 25-basis-point increase, and Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks had encouraged markets to treat a hike as likely. Waller added another influential view to a visibly divided committee rather than speaking for a settled consensus. Contracts linked to the September decision repriced to roughly 50% odds of a quarter-point move and reduced expected tightening through year-end to 34 basis points from as much as 41 basis points.

Services activity raised the hurdle for extending that rally. The ISM headline of 55.4 exceeded estimates near 54.2 and was the strongest expansion signal in six months. New orders rose 3.7 points to 60.9, their highest level since February 2023, while prices paid increased 2.3 points to 72.6. Supplier deliveries eased to 51.3 from 52.8 but remained above 50 for a 21st consecutive month. The final S&P Global services PMI told a compatible demand story at 56.5, up from 54.6, although it was revised below the 56.8 preliminary reading.

Labor within those surveys was much softer than demand. ISM employment stayed below the expansion threshold at 47.8 even as orders surged. Initial unemployment claims rose only 2,000 to 206,000 in the week ended August 29 after the prior week was revised to 204,000. The four-week average increased to 207,250, while continuing claims rose 8,000 to 1.779 million and their four-week average fell 5,000 to 1.78175 million. Layoffs have not broken higher, but hiring indicators are weak enough to leave the labor side of the mandate capable of constraining a hike.

The July trade report added a different kind of growth ambiguity. The goods-and-services deficit widened 24.4% to $88.6 billion from a revised $71.2 billion. Exports fell $6.6 billion, or 2.1%, to $310.7 billion, while imports increased $10.8 billion, or 2.8%, to $399.3 billion. The goods gap widened to $119.6 billion and the services surplus edged up to $31.0 billion. A larger deficit can subtract from gross domestic product, yet the composition was not simply weak final demand: capital-goods imports jumped $14.4 billion, including increases of $6.9 billion in computers and $6.6 billion in computer accessories. The report simultaneously points to a softer net-export contribution and sustained investment demand for technology equipment.

Waller's longer-horizon remarks prevent the front-end rally from becoming a complete duration thesis. He attributed part of the rise in Treasury yields to concern over the U.S. fiscal position, competition for capital from AI infrastructure and erosion of the safety and liquidity premium attached to government debt. Those forces have led him to raise his estimate of the neutral interest rate, implying that a given policy rate may restrain demand less than previously assumed. He placed federal debt around $40 trillion and the fiscal 2026 deficit near 6% of GDP, and argued that growth alone would not materially lower the debt burden unless structural deficits moved much closer to zero.

That view also limits what debt-management operations can accomplish. Waller did not expect doubling long-dated Treasury buybacks to provide much lasting relief; the first operation of at least $4 billion is due in September. Buybacks can improve liquidity in older securities, but his argument is that they do not remove the fiscal, inflation and competing-capital compensation demanded at the long end. The day's curve carried the same separation: 2-year yields responded most to the policy lean, while 10- and 30-year yields gave up only 2 basis points and remained substantially above week-earlier levels.

Activity in the cash market was concentrated where the reaction function changed most. Nominal-coupon trading reached $865.7 billion in original-face value, 6.1% more than the preceding session. Activity in maturities of 2 years or less increased 31.1% to $201.7 billion, and the greater-than-3-year through 5-year sector rose 16.4% to $243.2 billion. Those two-way volumes do not identify who bought or sold. They do show that the largest increase in turnover occurred in the maturities most exposed to the repricing of September and year-end policy.

## Japan's Yen Rally Gains Policy Support

The yen's 2% rise to 155.52 per dollar acquired a more durable explanation than renewed official intervention. Bank of Japan officials were reported to favor a 25-basis-point increase from the current 1% policy rate and to see no economic change large enough to require a 50-basis-point move. They also left the pace after September flexible if upside inflation risks persist. Swaps nearly fully priced a quarter-point increase and assigned about an 80% probability to another move in December. Short-covering and domestic hedging amplified the currency move, but the new information concerned the central bank's baseline and follow-through, not merely traders' fear that authorities might enter the market.

BOJ account data supplied the negative evidence. The central bank projected that its current account would fall by ¥410 billion for fiscal reasons, compared with money-broker estimates for a decline of roughly ¥700 billion. The gap was well below ¥729 billion, the smallest intervention since 2022, making another large official purchase of yen unlikely. That confirmation is important after Japan spent ¥15.4 trillion in the preceding intervention campaign. It means a move initially treated as possible official action was instead largely a market repricing of monetary policy and positioning.

Official pressure still helped shape that repricing. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Japan retained the same urgency toward the currency and reflected Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's view, although she emphasized that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had made no absolute demand in their meeting. BOJ board member Hajime Takata's earlier refusal to rule out larger or back-to-back increases had already widened the perceived distribution. The current clarification narrowed the first move toward 25 basis points without closing the door to a faster subsequent path. A failure to deliver any increase has consequently become more disruptive precisely because the standard move is now so heavily discounted.

The 30-year government-bond auction showed that higher yields can attract domestic demand without fixing a ceiling for super-long rates. The sale drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.79, below the previous 3.86 but above the 12-month average of 3.52. The 30-year yield had fallen as much as 10 basis points to 4.065% before the result, and futures retained gains afterward. Demand was broad enough to prevent the weak outcome investors had feared.

Auction quality was not unambiguously strong. The tail widened to 0.28 from 0.21, indicating a larger gap between average and lowest accepted prices. Buyers accepted supply above a 4% yield, but the wider tail left compensation for BOJ normalization and fiscal uncertainty unresolved. Record spending requests and the prospect of further policy increases still concentrate risk in the super-long sector even when life insurers regard 4% as investable.

A current signal from the Government Pension Investment Fund adds a potential source of demand rather than a completed allocation shift. Its management committee met on August 21, the first publicly announced August meeting in seven years, and revisited operating matters only five months after concluding that no portfolio review was needed. The ¥318 trillion fund still targets 25% each in domestic bonds, foreign bonds, Japanese equities and overseas equities. With the 10-year JGB yield having risen about 1 percentage point since March and briefly exceeded 3%, reconsidering the domestic-bond weight has become more plausible. The meeting itself does not establish that GPIF has changed its target.

The medium-term feedback into Treasuries runs through currency hedging as well as outright asset allocation. Large investors across six markets, including Japan, Canada and Taiwan, hedged only 41% of foreign-currency exposure as of June 30, the lowest proportion since at least 2015. A 5-percentage-point rise in hedge ratios would represent about $230 billion of transactions against the $4.6 trillion exposure measured in those markets. For yen-based investors, 3-month dollar hedge costs have fallen to 2.75% from 6% in October 2023, and Japanese investors hedged 41% of new foreign-bond purchases in the first half, down from 62% in 2024.

That positioning did not cause Thursday's Treasury rally, and the survey covers only part of global holdings. It does define an asymmetry if BOJ tightening narrows interest-rate differentials and the dollar ceases to cushion risk-off periods. Japanese investors can retain U.S. bonds while selling dollars forward, so stronger hedging need not mean immediate Treasury liquidation. It can, however, weaken the currency return attached to dollar assets and alter the marginal economics of foreign-duration demand just as domestic JGB yields become more competitive.

## Energy Risk Raises Different Policy Hurdles

Europe entered the heating season with an unusually small energy buffer. More than 100 terawatt-hours of gas, worth over €7 billion at prevailing prices, would be needed to reach even the European Union's lowest 75% storage target. Achieving that level requires an injection pace not seen this late in the season since the 2022 energy crisis. Gas prices held steady after rising 10% in three days, but low inventories leave the region exposed to cold weather, aggressive Chinese buying, pipeline outages or disruptions to U.S. liquefied-natural-gas supply. That physical constraint keeps an inflation premium in European duration even when crude's daily advance moderates.

The European Central Bank's near-term step has become more certain while the endpoint remains disputed. All 65 economists in a current poll expected the next decision to raise the deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.50%, up from an 83% share in August. About 91% expected 2.50% at year-end, and 78% expected the rate to remain there through mid-2027. Interest-rate futures, by contrast, priced another increase beyond that move. The difference is not about the immediate direction; it is about whether an energy-led inflation impulse becomes persistent enough to extend the cycle.

August activity and prices leave room for that disagreement. The euro-area services PMI eased only marginally to 51.6 from 51.7, and the composite index held at 52.0. Aggregate export orders increased for the first time in four and a half years as manufacturing demand offset weaker overseas services business. Services employment grew at its fastest pace in eight months, producing the first month of net private-sector job creation in 2026. Input costs and output charges in services both reached three-month highs, while composite output-price inflation stopped falling. Headline inflation at 3.3% and a stalled disinflation trend justify the expected move; neither alone proves the additional increase embedded in markets.

Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill described the same energy shock through the cost of waiting. He argued that an early Bank Rate increase could prevent temporary inflation pressure from becoming persistent and reduce the need for more aggressive tightening later. Pill was one of three Monetary Policy Committee members who favored an increase in July. Futures assigned little more than a 15% chance to a quarter-point move in September but more than 70% by November. His intervention broadens the case for action without showing that the committee has converged on its timing.

British duration is already drawing a new buyer response at historically high yields. Purchases on Freetrade's bond platform reached their highest number and value of 2026 on Tuesday, and Hargreaves Lansdown recorded its busiest day for gilt buying since May 15. A 5.375% bond due in 2056 and low-coupon issues due in 2028 and 2061 were among the most active. Retail investors still own less than 4% of outstanding bonds, so this flow cannot absorb the sovereign market by itself. It does show that 10-year yields around 5.2% and 30-year yields near 5.8% are drawing tax-sensitive household demand after the global selloff.

Malaysia delivered a subtler but realized hawkish turn. Bank Negara Malaysia held its overnight policy rate at 2.75%, as 20 of 22 economists expected, but removed the description of the stance as “appropriate” after using that word in every decision since September 2025. Ringgit swaps added 14 basis points of tightening over the following 12 months and moved to nearly 50% odds of a cumulative 50-basis-point increase, from pricing close to one 25-basis-point move before the decision. Growth near 5% for 2026, including a 6% second quarter, gives the bank room to respond if July's subdued 1.8% inflation is displaced by stronger demand or energy pass-through.

Turkey's August inflation release moved in the opposite direction at the margin. Annual price growth slowed to 31.5% from 31.8%, slightly below the 31.6% consensus, and monthly inflation of 1.84% was below the 1.92% estimate despite edging up from 1.78%. The 2-year lira-bond yield fell 14 basis points to 39.6%. A cut became more plausible after funding normalized back to the 37% policy rate from an effective 40%, but sticky core inflation, renewed energy pressure and weaker inflation expectations make immediate easing contested. The same oil shock that keeps the ECB and BOE alert can delay a Turkish cut even as headline disinflation continues.

Poland and Hungary further separate the regional paths. Polish policymaker Iwona Duda said the 3.75% rate was likely to remain unchanged through the rest of 2026, even though forward agreements priced roughly three quarter-point increases over 12 months. August inflation reached a 14-month high of 3.4%, close to the upper edge of the 2.5% target's tolerance band, and expiring fuel-price caps and higher fertilizer costs could push it above the band. Duda saw no immediate need to tighten but rejected expectations for near-term cuts.

Hungary was reported to be preparing to pause after three consecutive 25-basis-point cuts, leaving its benchmark at 5.5%, while lowering the inflation target to 2.5% from 3%. The forint strengthened as much as 1.5% against the euro and government-bond yields fell because the target change reinforced the new government's euro-convergence agenda. July inflation of 1.2% creates space for a lower target without immediate tightening. A projected 2026 budget deficit of 7.5% of GDP and Fitch's focus on a credible debt path keep the bond response dependent on fiscal delivery rather than the inflation target alone.

Australia illustrates how the global duration shock can outrun domestic differentiation. Its 10-year yield rose about 30 basis points over the month through Wednesday to a 15-year high of 5.25%, more than peer moves, despite triple-A ratings from all three major agencies and public debt below U.S. and U.K. levels. Foreign funds owned 51% of government debt in March, up from 46% one year earlier, and the hedged sovereign index still returned 0.3% in 2026 versus losses of 0.7% for Treasuries and 0.6% for global government bonds. Stronger credit quality can support relative performance, but high correlation with U.S. rates leaves the market exposed until the global inflation and supply premium stabilizes.

## Pakistan Reopens the Sovereign Funding Window

Pakistan completed the clearest current demonstration that hard-currency access remains open for a low-rated sovereign. It raised a record $3 billion in two tranches: $1.75 billion of 5-year bonds at 7.75% and $1.25 billion of 10-year debt at 8.25%. Orders approached $6 billion, and the risk premium tightened about 25 basis points during marketing. The sale broadly matched yields on similarly rated sovereign debt even though Moody's B3 rating remains six notches below investment grade.

The funding purpose matters more than the headline orderbook. Pakistan faces about $22 billion of external financing needs and intends to repay expensive short-term obligations, extend maturities and reduce rollover risk. The United Arab Emirates recently declined to roll over $3 billion after seven years of renewals, requiring replacement support from Saudi Arabia. Pakistan also requested refinancing of a $1.3 billion commercial loan from China, its largest creditor with more than $25 billion outstanding, and is considering sukuk and yuan bonds within a three-year funding strategy. The completed transaction replaces part of reliance on bilateral deposits with term market debt; it does not remove the wider external-funding requirement.

The broad close was receptive to that distinction. Hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly, while Pakistan's 2031 note edged to 99.65 cents. Credit-rating upgrades and an IMF program improved access, and global high-yield premiums near multi-decade lows helped execution. A near-two-times covered orderbook at 7.75%-8.25% still shows the price required to finance reform progress in a market where core government yields remain high.

India faces the inverse problem: foreign-currency mobilization created excess domestic liquidity. Banks gathered a record $127 billion in Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits under an incentive program, and more than $136 billion including related foreign-currency loans. The response helped the rupee and gave banks a cheaper deposit base, but direct swaps with the Reserve Bank of India lifted banking-system liquidity to a record 9.7 trillion rupees, about $102.66 billion. The program ended on August 31, one month early, because inflows greatly exceeded the initial ambition of at least $80 billion.

Bank executives have now proposed dollar-rupee sell-buy swaps to drain that surplus rather than a higher cash-reserve ratio. Swaps with maturities of as much as one year could match roughly $45 billion of short-dollar positions in the RBI's forward book that are estimated to mature within a year. The instrument would absorb rupees while rolling foreign-exchange exposure; bond sales and a reserve-requirement increase remain alternatives. Banks opposed the reserve route because it would compress margins. The choice will determine whether excess liquidity supports money markets and bonds or is sterilized through the currency book.

The Philippines showed how a weaker currency can instead constrain planned local supply. The Treasury is reassessing a 5-year jumbo bond that formed part of 380 billion pesos of September issuance. Inflation slowed for three months but remained 6.2% in July, more than twice the annual target, while the peso reached a record low as the Middle East conflict lifted oil costs. More than 100 billion pesos of retail Treasury bonds mature in September and another 50 billion pesos in October, so canceling the large sale would complicate refinancing and market liquidity. Proceeding would lock in a higher interest bill. Demand at the latest 5-year auction was only 1.2 times the offered amount, down from 3.1 times at the prior comparable sale.

Venezuela's defaulted bonds moved higher because the prospective resource base available to a restructuring changed. Sovereign notes due in 2027 reached 54 cents on the dollar, near a four-month high, after an agreement gave the United States control over more than 65 billion barrels of proven reserves. Including unpaid accrued interest, current prices imply recovery of less than one-third of claims. Analysts see production potentially reaching 1.5 million barrels a day within one or two years, while Chevron has committed $7 billion over five years to more than double its Venezuelan output.

The rework could still become the largest sovereign restructuring on record. One estimate places total claims as high as $229 billion if commercial PDVSA debt and local-currency obligations are included, with potential haircuts ranging from 26% under a political transition to 83% under continuity. The current bond rally reflects a higher probability of future dollar revenue, not agreement on debt sustainability, creditor perimeter or deployed capital. Oil investment has improved the numerator in recovery models before the government has disclosed the denominator.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva supplied the system-level limit to these idiosyncratic successes. She warned that higher advanced-economy yields, persistent energy inflation and competition for capital from AI issuance could reverse improvements in low-income and emerging-market debt sustainability. She still described markets as orderly and pointed to Senegal as a test of efforts to accelerate the Group of 20 Common Framework. Pakistan's sale, India's liquidity surplus and Venezuela's recovery hopes show that capital remains available; the terms and the route through which it arrives now matter more than a single emerging-market beta.

## Heavy Supply Exposes the Weakest Balance Sheets

Broad U.S. credit spreads did not move even as the financing calendar became more demanding. Average investment-grade yields exceeded 5.5%, while spreads remained below 80 basis points for much of the week. Dealers' central estimate for September issuance was about $215 billion, above the $207.5 billion monthly record set one year earlier; individual forecasts ranged from roughly $190 billion to $250 billion. Issuers set monthly records in four of 2026's first eight months, including the latest three. High Treasury yields are encouraging borrowers with 2027 needs to advance funding while spread compensation is still contained.

The pressure is as much about investor concentration as aggregate capacity. Technology companies are financing an expanding AI buildout, and repeated large deals raise the share of individual issuers in benchmark portfolios. Many investment-grade mandates limit a single company's weight to 3%-5%. Even if the largest technology borrowers remain below those thresholds, another heavy month can force investors to compare incremental exposure with a growing range of alternatives. Stable broad spreads therefore coexist with a rising clearing hurdle for issuers that arrive after balance sheets have already absorbed substantial supply.

ByteDance demonstrated that bank capacity is still available at scale. The company secured a $29.6 billion dollar loan after initially seeking $20 billion, making it Asia's second-largest dollar-denominated borrowing of 2026. The increase followed strong bank commitments and will support an accelerated AI investment program. It is a completed financing with a substantially larger final size, not merely evidence that technology borrowers intend to spend.

Other issuers are diversifying currency and security. Public Storage is discussing about C$500 million of 7-year bonds at an initial spread near 95 basis points over Canadian government debt, its first financing in the currency, after completing a C$1.2 billion acquisition of 68 Canadian facilities. Its U.S. senior unsecured debt is rated A2/A. AirAsia, at the opposite end of the risk spectrum, said as much as $1 billion of international debt and 700 million ringgit of local facilities would refinance expensive pandemic-era obligations rather than fund operating losses.

AirAsia's existing stack shows why that distinction requires scrutiny. It arranged a $230 million private-credit bond in April backed by route revenue and borrowed $443 million in 2024 from funds including Ares at coupons as high as 11%. A lack of fuel hedging and limited ability to pass higher jet-fuel costs to price-sensitive travelers contributed to a 527 million-ringgit quarterly net loss, the largest in four years. Refinancing can extend maturities and reduce interest drag; it must still clear against weaker operating cash generation and an equity price that has fallen 64% since the Iran war began.

Cerba Healthcare has moved beyond refinancing preparation into a court-supervised process. The EQT-backed laboratory company requested French conciliation proceedings for a debt pile around €5 billion after lenders had already described the capital structure as unsustainable. Net debt exceeded €4.9 billion, or 9 times trailing earnings, while cash at June was about €108 million. A €100 million sponsor loan provided liquidity, and creditors extended a grace period on interest payments to November. Second-quarter EBITDA grew about 12% to more than €122 million and revenue rose 2% to €469 million, but those gains have not repaired leverage or the tariff uncertainty surrounding French reimbursement rates.

CSN offered a contrasting case in which governance change improved the market's confidence in deleveraging. Benjamin Steinbruch stepped down immediately as chief executive after more than two decades and became chairman, with former Vale head Fabio Schvartsman taking the operating role. CSN is seeking about $2.9 billion from sales of cement and infrastructure stakes. Its 11% bonds due in 2030 rose 2.25 cents to 80.5, while the shares gained as much as 20%. The reaction reflects greater confidence that asset disposals and capital-structure repair will proceed, not a completed reduction in debt.

Municipal borrowers show how dedicated revenue and operating pressure can diverge within the same market. New York's Metropolitan Transportation Authority disclosed a $785 million issue backed by taxes on property sales of at least $2 million. The levy is expected to raise nearly $400 million in 2026 and about $350 million annually from 2027 through 2030, against approximately $150 million of yearly debt service once the new bonds are issued. Moody's rates the structure A1 and S&P recently raised it to AA-. The transaction will exhaust a statutory cap on annual principal and interest for these securities, making the pledged tax base rather than broader MTA operations the central protection.

Chicago's new forecast places more pressure directly on its operating balance. Mayor Brandon Johnson projected an $882 million corporate-fund deficit for 2027 as bond payments, cost-of-living adjustments, commodity inflation and lower tax-increment-financing surpluses raise expenses. An $85 million hole remains in the current budget after weaker-than-expected revenue from measures including the proposed sale of debt collections. The city plans a $364 million supplemental pension payment next year and is using refinancing savings and residual pandemic reserves to address the nearer shortfall. Those measures provide liquidity but do not identify the recurring revenue needed to close the larger 2027 gap.

China's onshore ratings structure creates a separate form of spread opacity. Nearly 90% of more than 6,500 credit-bond issuers carry domestic ratings of AA or higher, compared with 4.4% in the United States. S&P highlighted the possibility that an issuer rated B globally, a category with a cited 15.34% 5-year cumulative potential default rate, could receive AAA treatment for a panda bond. The People's Bank of China has pressed local agencies since April to reduce top-rating concentration, prompting downgrades and withdrawals. Better differentiation across a 37 trillion-yuan market could widen issuer dispersion even if aggregate funding remains available to foreign borrowers.

These transactions explain the still-flat U.S. spread indices without equating flatness with uniform financing conditions. ByteDance enlarged a bank loan, Public Storage is opening a new currency pool and the MTA has a ring-fenced tax pledge. AirAsia must refinance through weak earnings, Cerba is negotiating under court supervision, CSN is relying on asset-sale execution and Chicago has an unresolved operating gap. Benchmark yields are common to all of them; collateral, revenue dedication, ranking and cash generation determine which balance sheets can absorb them.

## Forward Market Significance

The August employment report at 8:30 a.m. ET on September 4 is the first test of whether Waller's conditional patience can survive a labor surprise. Payrolls are expected to increase 56,000 after a 23,000 decline, unemployment is expected to remain at 4.1% and average hourly earnings are expected to rise 0.3% month over month after 0.1%. Weak hiring with stable or softer wages would reinforce the 2-year rally and move the September distribution further toward a hold. A stronger payroll gain or firmer wage result, particularly with unemployment unchanged, would reconnect the services-demand signal to the case for tightening.

Inflation and duration absorption then converge in the following week. Headline and core producer prices are each expected to rise 0.3% month over month on September 10, followed by August consumer prices on September 11. The Treasury's 3-, 10- and 30-year auctions and an anticipated rebound in corporate supply will reveal whether investors accept current yields while the inflation result is still unsettled. Benign price breadth with orderly auctions would allow the distinction between near-term Fed patience and a structural term premium to persist. Sticky non-energy inflation or weak bidding would pull the policy and supply risks back together, limiting long-end gains even if payroll growth slows.

Global duration faces a shared policy-sequencing test through two different central banks. The ECB's September 10 decision is widely expected to lift the deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.50%; guidance on whether energy and service prices require anything beyond that move will determine whether market pricing or the economists' one-and-done path is closer to the Governing Council. The BOJ on September 18 has the sharper binary because a quarter-point increase is nearly fully discounted. A standard hike with credible flexibility on subsequent moves would support the yen and test whether JGB demand can absorb normalization without another global spillover. Delay, or guidance that closes off follow-through, would challenge the policy foundation of the yen's rally and revive the intervention risk that account data ruled out this week.
